clue.text: Delighted, being very close to earth

definitions.meaning: taken literally, the phrase puts you right on the planet's surface

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: standing on the globe is about as close to earth as you can get.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means elated; read literally it means resting on the planet's surface.

clue.text: Just started to make a point, not in a rush

parts.note: runners who have just started are 'off', as in 'they're off'
a peak is a pointed summit

explanation.surface: Someone who has only just begun to argue a point is taking their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' is the rush hour; outside it travel is cheaper and quieter.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak travel happens outside the busy rush hours.

clue.text: Paper in a state for a while?

definitions.meaning: a newspaper, here the one printing this very crossword
a state of affairs lasting a period

explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own newspaper supplies the first sense; the second is the plural noun for periods with a particular character.
explanation.definitionFit: The London newspaper is a paper, and periods marked by some condition are spoken of as hard or good days of a kind.

clue.text: Neophyte'beginning to learn about plastic

indicators.note: about here signals that the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of the word learn supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: A newcomer is starting to learn about plastics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NEOPHYTE plus the L that 'beginning to learn' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Polythene is a common plastic used for bags and sheeting.

clue.text: Be angry with fellow that's picked up bird?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking a word up lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Someone seethes at a man who has collected a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' works as a reversal only because this is a down entry, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume is to seethe with anger.

clue.text: Suspend deliveries, given problem arising?

parts.note: to suspend something is to hang it
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

explanation.surface: Someone halts deliveries because a problem has come up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an OVER is a set of six balls bowled from one end; 'deliveries' sounds like parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: The after-effect of heavy drinking is a problem that arises the next morning.

clue.text: Failing to come right out

parts.note: something that does not come out right has turned out in error

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out right' means turn out correctly; failing to do so is the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fails to come out right is incorrect, the opposite of correct.

clue.text: Blush, collecting trophy, half resigned to being passed over again

indicators.note: one word collecting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to blush is to redden

indicators.note: half of the word trophy is its first three letters

explanation.surface: Someone flushes on receiving a trophy, half reconciled to being overlooked again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' inserts half the trophy into the blush. 'Passed over' reads as overlooked, but here means walked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Trodden ground has been walked on; walked over a second time it is trodden once more.

clue.text: Ironic about serious assault suggested hanging?

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps round it

parts.note: dry humour is ironic and understated
rape is a grave sexual assault

explanation.surface: A wry remark about a violent crime hints at execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the ironic word around the assault. 'Hanging' suggests the gallows but means curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: Draped fabric such as curtains is a hanging.

clue.text: He'd raise personal issues with special care

definitions.text: He'd raise personal issues with special care

parts.words: He'd raise personal issues with special care
parts.note: issues are offspring, so raising one's own issues is bringing up children

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' sounds like topics to bring up, but means offspring, which a devoted father raises.
explanation.definitionFit: A man devoted to his wife and children brings up his offspring carefully.

clue.text: Drunken sot knocked back first-class vintage port

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger into a new order
knocked back means the letters run in reverse order, as a drink is knocked back

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 taken as the letter I

explanation.surface: A drunk downs a top-quality old port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' shuffles SOT to OST; 'knocked back' turns AI (A1) to IA. Ostia was ancient Rome's port, so 'vintage' means old, not wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the harbour town of ancient Rome, a port of great age.

clue.text: Imitation of bankers, at Zurich gathering

indicators.note: the words gathered together hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A fake made by Swiss bankers meeting in Zurich.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means a substitute or imitation, often an inferior one.

clue.text: In a haze, kiss sweetheart, presenting a flower

indicators.note: the kiss is put in the haze, splitting it

parts.note: fog is a haze
X is a kiss at the end of a letter
love is a term for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: In a dreamy daze, a lover kisses their darling and offers a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sends the kiss inside the haze, and the sweetheart follows; a lover's daze is the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove is a tall wild plant with purple bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Typical Scot, as you might say, out of it, not 'going to work

definitions.text: Typical Scot, as you might say, out of it, not 'going to work

parts.words: Typical Scot, as you might say, out of it, not 'going to work
parts.note: a Scot in a kilt might be jokingly called a kilt-wearer; and something out of order is said to be out of this word

explanation.walkthrough: Two jokes: a kilt-wearing Scot as one who kilts, and the idiom 'out of kilter', meaning not working properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilter means good working order, used mainly in the phrase for things not working properly.

clue.text: He has grounds to justify' his occupation

definitions.text: He has grounds to justify' his occupation

parts.words: He has grounds to justify' his occupation
parts.note: 'grounds' means reasons, but also estates of property

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' suggests reasons for a job; read as estates, it describes someone who owns and occupies land.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor of estates literally holds grounds which he occupies.

clue.text: Leaves without bags — they can be stored here

definitions.text: Leaves without bags — they can be stored here

parts.words: Leaves without bags — they can be stored here
parts.note: loose leaves of the drink, not in teabags, are kept in a small tin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about departing, but means loose tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small container keeps loose leaf tea fresh.

clue.text: Ah! Topical cook prepared sausage

indicators.note: the letters are cooked and prepared, worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a cook gets a sausage ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook prepared' rearranges the letters of AH TOPICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage.

clue.text: With, awful din muffled, could possibly go to' sleep this time?

indicators.note: a sound muffled is wrapped up, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: might means could possibly

indicators.note: an awful version of the word is a jumbled one

explanation.surface: With the dreadful racket quietened, one might at last get to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' scrambles the din to DNI and 'muffled' wraps the could-possibly word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is a traditional hour for going to bed.

clue.text: Yours truly's keeping epic movie for a Christmas treat

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, so what belongs to yours truly is mine

indicators.note: a movie here is read as moving, so the letters move

explanation.surface: I'm keeping hold of an epic film to enjoy over Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movie' gives CEPI from the epic, and 'keeping' holds it inside the possessive; the film is a false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pastry filled with dried fruit is eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Nobleman who, in France, is into spoils (of war?)

indicators.note: one word is into another when it goes inside it

parts.note: mars means spoils or damages
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat is taking a share of the spoils of war.
explanation.walkthrough: '(of war?)' is a playful nod: MARS is also the Roman god of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking below a duke.

clue.text: Starts to, break into skating, almost superhuman

indicators.note: the starts of the next words supply their first letters
almost means the final letter is lost

parts.note: a skater is on ice

explanation.surface: A beginner breaking into figure skating is nearly superhuman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ON ICE to ONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bionic powers come from electronic body parts, making someone more than human.

clue.text: Hide, whenever in a state

indicators.note: one word is placed in another

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation of California, a US state
once can mean whenever, as in 'once you arrive, call'

explanation.surface: Keep out of sight whenever you are agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' suggests being upset, but the state is California.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to hide it from view.

clue.text: Settling on jumper, smart?

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: Sitting down on a sweater feels uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a sweater, but is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch for the night when they come in to rest.

clue.text: Fool deleted article on Belgian community

indicators.note: deleted means the named piece is cut from the word

parts.note: Antwerp is a Belgian city
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An idiot removed a story about a Belgian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but is the grammatical word AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person.

clue.text: Scott and Janis put together, comprising retrospective LP

indicators.note: one word comprising another contains it

parts.note: to join things is to put them together

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A retrospective album pairs two musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott Joplin was the ragtime composer and Janis Joplin the rock singer; 'retrospective' turns the LP round inside the joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both musicians share this surname.

clue.text: When we may arrive, having brief time in genuine hold-up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding a word up lifts it to read upwards
in tells us the short time sits inside the word for genuine, between its letters

parts.note: real means genuine
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A delay meant we arrived after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T inside REAL to give RETAL; 'hold-up' turns it upward. 'Hold-up' looks like a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: We may turn up at some subsequent time.

clue.text: Yielded under pressure, and made a donation

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense covers collapsing under strain and handing something over as a gift.

clue.text: Bones at risk, if you finally lean out?

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of the word you
out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Your bones are at risk if you lean out too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LEAN after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is a forearm bone; these are the plural.

clue.text: Promising security system

parts.note: an arrangement that promises safety or protection, like a warranty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Security system' suggests alarms, but means a formal pledge of protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a formal pledge that ensures something will be done.

clue.text: Jam part of gun, and look to a last resort

parts.note: a scrape is a jam, a tight spot
the barrel is the tube of a gun

explanation.surface: Clear a blocked gun barrel, as a desperate measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' reads as a verb about blocking a gun, but is a noun for a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Having to use the dregs of what is left means resorting to the last option.
